fileNameIsDeliberate: This file is named shade-symbiants.json even though a Shade wears NO symbiants. That is on purpose: the AODB app maps [slug]-symbiants.json onto the "Implants & Symbiants" tab, so naming it this way makes the Shade page render its Spirits with no renderer change. Read every "symbiant" label on that tab as "Spirit".
summary: A SHADE WEARS NO SYMBIANTS AND NO IMPLANTS. In all 13 implant slots it wears SPIRITS instead - the client's own ItemClass 5, 844 templates, 842 of them ToWear-locked to Profession 15. Verified from the data both ways: running the symbiant extractor with --prof 15 returns 14 usable symbiant templates out of 1,462 wearable ones, and 12 of those 14 are the known unlocked Xan Artillery-unit anomaly (ids 278908-278919, which carry no profession lock at all, unlike every other Artillery item) plus two unlocked one-offs (245306 Brumal Chest Symbiant of Endurance, 245895 Head Symbiant of the Love Child). There is no Shade symbiant line to pick. Spirits differ from symbiants in three ways that change how you play: they need NO surgery clinic (their ToWear carries no Treatment requirement at all - only Level, Agility, Sense, Profession and the expansion bit), they CANNOT be over-equipped, and a Spirit buffs more skills than an implant of the same QL. You get ordinary Spirits with the Spirit Siphon nano (id 297342): bring a target below 20% health, cast it, kill the target, loot the Soul Capsule, open it. The tier prefix (Bitter ... Wistful) is a QL LABEL, not a drop location - the 34-step ladder runs QL1/level 1 to QL300/level 219 and you farm a tier by siphoning mobs around that level, not by camping a named boss. Endgame is the Legacy-of-the-Xan ladder: Xan Beta Spirits (QL250 only) drop in the three LoX encounters, and you CRAFT the Alpha from a high-QL ordinary Spirit plus the matching Beta, then combine two Alphas of the same slot into a Combined Alpha. See farmingRuns for the location-by-location plan and acquisitionBySlot for the per-slot ladder.

substitution.claim: A Shade wears no symbiants at all. It wears Spirits.
substitution.why: The Shade is the one profession in Anarchy Online whose implant slots do not take implants or symbiants. The client states the reason in its own item text.
evidence: items.ocp / tools/mp-symbiant-extractor --prof 15: 120,842 templates read, 1,464 match "Symbiant", 1,462 are wearable, and only 14 come back usable by profession 15.

Twelve of those 14 are ids 278908-278919, the Xan [slot] Symbiant, Artillery Unit set - they carry an EMPTY profession lock in items.ocp while every other Artillery symbiant carries the Soldier/Fixer/Agent/Adventurer/Trader lock. That is a client-data anomaly, not a Shade permission.
The other two are 245306 Brumal Chest Symbiant of Endurance and 245895 Head Symbiant of the Love Child, also unlocked one-offs.

items.ocp id 218576 "Whispering Spirit", client description: "...put it into the Right-Arm IMPLANT slot. Note: Shades can not use implants, as all the other professions. Their physique is to fragile for them to survive mechanical pieces inside. Instead the Shades of the World use captured spirits. The Spirits can be installed and taken out without the aid of any machinery. The drawback of this is that they do not accept to be overequipped."

items.ocp filtered on ItemClass == 5 with --prof 15: 844 templates, ALL usable, 842 explicitly ToWear-locked to Shade. The other two are 215259 "Shade Implant Test item" (a development leftover) and 305506 "Ethereal Embrace".

Regular implants are ItemClass 3: 44,060 of them exist in items.ocp and NOT ONE carries a profession lock, so the Shade prohibition is a client/server rule rather than an item criterion - which is exactly why it has to be stated on the page.
ao-universe: "Unlike the other 13 professions... Shades cannot utilize standard implants"; wiki.aodb.us/wiki/Shade: "In their place, you will find trapped Spirits".

Requirement shape, read from the data: Xan Right Limb Spirit of Power - Alpha (id 279217) ToWear = Expansion BitAnd 128 (Legacy of the Xan), Level > 218, Agility > 1275, Sense > 1275, Profession EqualTo 15. NO Treatment requirement - which is the mechanical difference from every symbiant and every implant in the game.
substitution.appImpact: None needed. The Implants & Symbiants tab renders whatever [slug]-symbiants.json contains, so the Spirits appear with no code change. The only cosmetic wrinkle is that the table heading still reads "Best-in-slot symbiants"; an optional one-line additive renderer tweak can print sy.itemNoun when present.

unitChoice.recommendedUnit: n/a - a Shade has no symbiant unit line
unitChoice.why: There is no Artillery / Control / Extermination / Infantry / Support choice to make. Every Spirit is Shade-only and the choice inside the system is by SPIRIT TYPE per slot, not by unit line. ao-universe gives the suffix meanings: Essence = 1-3 basic abilities, Knowledge = nano skills plus nano pool/max nano, Strength = offensive, Weakness = defensive, with Offence/Defence/Clear Thought/Insight/True Seeing/Understanding as named variants of those four.
unitChoice.typesPerSlotFromTheData: See catalog.tiers[].spirits[].spiritType - the type list is derived from the item names in items.ocp, not copied from a guide.

xanAlphaNote: Endgame path: farm ordinary Spirits up the tier ladder with Spirit Siphon to Tragic (QL250) / Wistful (QL300); run the three Legacy-of-the-Xan encounters for the QL250 Xan Betas; CRAFT the Alpha from [ordinary Spirit of the matching type] + [matching Xan Beta]; bump it toward QL300 by injecting 3-4 more of the same Beta (or start from a QL300 base and usually hit QL300 at once); then combine two different Alphas of the same slot into a Combined Alpha that keeps both skill sets. An Alpha is NODROP once made, so build it on the Shade that will wear it. Feet is the only slot with no combined upgrade.

alphaCrafting.what: Xan Alpha Spirits cannot be looted. Each is crafted, and NODROP once assembled - the Beta's own client description warns "If upgraded to Alpha type it becomes NoDrop."
alphaCrafting.recipe: [ordinary Spirit of the matching type, high QL] + [matching Xan Spirit ... - Beta] = [Xan Spirit ... - Alpha].
qlBehaviour: Low-QL base Spirits produce a QL250 Alpha; you "bump" it toward QL300 by injecting more of the SAME Beta, typically 3-4 injections.
Using a QL300 (Wistful) ordinary Spirit as the base often reaches QL300 immediately.
Two DIFFERENT Alphas of the same slot combine into a Combined Alpha that keeps both skill sets plus extra bonuses.
CRITICAL: the Combined Alpha takes the TARGET item's QL. Put the higher-QL Spirit in the target slot, and bump AFTER combining, not before.
A Combined Alpha can still be bumped afterwards with one of its component Betas.
alphaCrafting.betaDropTable: Betas exist at QL250 only. Per slot: Eye / Left Arm / Right Wrist / Waist = Ground Chief Vortexx; Head / Chest / Left Wrist / Left Hand = The Alien Threat (Mitaar Hero); Right Arm / Right Hand / Feet = The Xan (12-man); Ear = the Arid Rift quest line; Legs = the Neretva Canyons quest line. The ao-universe page footnotes that Ear and Legs Betas are also reported from The Xan 12-man. This mapping was produced twice independently on this project and agreed on all 13 slots.
alphaCrafting.tradeskillRequirement: unknown - the ao-universe recipe page names no tradeskill and no skill level for the combine, and no other allowed source gives one. Deliberately not guessed. Use the in-game Tradeskill window to preview the result.

_verification.namesAndIds: Every id in this file was re-verified against E:/Funcom/attic/extracted-client-data/itemnames.sql; the generator asserts that the name in the raw dump equals the itemnames.sql name for the same id.
_verification.statsAndReqs: QL, keyBonuses and reqs extracted from items.ocp (OMNICELL-CONTENT v3, client 18.8.50_EP1) with tools/mp-symbiant-extractor --prof 15 --itemclass 5; stat numbers mapped from AOSharp.Common Stat.cs; ToWear = equip reqs, funcType 53045 = worn stat bonuses.
_verification.itemClassFilter: ItemClass == 5 (stat 76) is the client's own Spirit class and is what this extraction filters on. A NAME filter on "Spirit" would miss 215259 "Shade Implant Test item" and 305506 "Ethereal Embrace", and the playbook's "--match \"Spirit of\" returns 774" figure undercounts the real total of 844.
_verification.professionLock: ToWear stat-60 EqualTo 15 on 842 of the 844; the two unlocked ones are 215259 (a development test item) and 305506.
_verification.noDropFlags: NODROP/Unique read from the client, not a website: items.ocp Stats entry 0 ("Flags"), bit 26 = NoDrop, bit 27 = Unique (OmniCell.Enums/ItemFlags.cs). All 13 best-in-slot Alphas are NODROP. Whispering Spirit (218576) is NODROP and Unique.
_verification.expansionGate: ToWear stat 389 BitAnd. bit 2 = Shadowlands on the ordinary ladder and on the Fabricated/Prototype families; bit 128 = Legacy of the Xan on every Xan Beta and Alpha.
_verification.crossCheck: The 34-step tier ladder derived from items.ocp (adjective, QL, level requirement, ability requirement) was checked against the independent QL/level/ability table on the ao-universe Shade guide: all 34 prefixes and all 34 QLs agree. Ability figures can differ by exactly 1 because items.ocp stores Operator.GreaterThan(v) while the guide prints v. The 13-slot Xan Beta drop mapping was likewise produced twice, independently, and agreed on all 13 slots.
_verification.bestInSlotSelection: The BiS picks are a stated judgement, not a copied tier list: within each slot, take the QL300 Combined Alpha whose bonuses land on the skills a Shade actually uses (Piercing, Multi Melee, Sneak Attack, Fast Attack, Dimach, Melee Init, the evades, Add All Off/Def, Max Health). Every bonus figure quoted in the "why" text is read from the item template.

_unverified: No formula ties siphoned Spirit QL to mob level. The rule the sources actually state is "kill monsters whose level is around the QL you want your Spirits to be". Treat the per-tier camps as level-band guidance.

The chance that a Soul Capsule actually contains a Spirit is not documented. A patch note records "Soul Capsules will have a higher chance of having a Spirit inside" as a past fix; a player estimate of 25-50% exists but is not an official figure and is not asserted here.
The tradeskill and skill level required to perform an Alpha combine are UNKNOWN - the ao-universe recipe page names neither.

Whispering Spirit (id 218576): no page on ao-universe.com, wiki.aodb.us or forums.funcom.com documents it. Its acquisition rests entirely on the client's own description text ("given to you by the Shades of the Independent Professionals Society in Jobe"). Do not confuse it with "Whispering Visitant" (an Adonis mob) or "Whispering Soul Stone" (a Jobe Research Training Facility drop).

Ethereal Embrace (id 305506) and Ethereal Spirit of Berserker Rage (id 260763): no allowed source documents either. The allowed sources do document an "Ethereal Implant of Berserker Rage" from the Inferno quest line, but that is a symbiant and nothing connects the two. Left unknown.

The Fabricated and Prototype Spirit families (34 templates each): the allowed sources document only the SYMBIANT counterparts (cash-shop Explorers' Packs and the symbiant Daily Reward respectively). Nothing states the Spirit versions share those sources, so they are left unknown.
Spirit Siphon's cooldown length and its stated Dimach-skill scaling are not quantified anywhere on the allowed sources.
215259 "Shade Implant Test item" is a development leftover with no profession lock and no description. It is carried in the catalogue for completeness and marked not obtainable.

The best-in-slot rows are the QL300 Combined Alphas. Every Shade below level 219 / Agility 1276 / Sense 1276 wears something lower - use the tier ladder in catalog.tiers, which carries the exact level and ability requirement of every step.

farmingMethods.spiritSiphon: Spirit Siphon (nano 297342, nano line SpiritDrain, Shade-only, Shadowlands-gated) has been a NANO rather than a usable item since patch 18.8.53; it is granted at character creation and is otherwise bought from the Shade nano vendor in a Fair Trade shop (ao-universe names the ICC Fair Trade nano shops on RK5/RK19 and the Arete Landing starter quest; a patch note adds the Jobe Harbor IPS). ao-universe states it is based on Dimach skill. Mechanic: bring a target below 20% health (the quest text says "< 21% health"), cast Spirit Siphon - it deals 1% of the target's health as damage - kill it, and loot the Soul Capsule from the corpse; opening the capsule may yield a Spirit. A capsule does NOT always contain one (a patch note records "Soul Capsules will have a higher chance of having a Spirit inside" as a fix). Spirit-type mobs in Shadowlands can also drop Spirits directly, and the nano works on Rubi-Ka mobs too, not only Shadowlands ones. IMPORTANT: no allowed source gives a formula tying Spirit QL to mob level. The rule of thumb the sources actually state is "kill monsters whose level is around the QL you want your Spirits to be", and ao-universe indexes its camp table by "approximate level of the spirit monster". Treat the per-tier camps below as level-band guidance, not as a formula.
farmingMethods.xanAlpha: Legacy of the Xan spirits come in Beta (QL250 only) and Alpha (QL250-300). Betas drop in the three LoX encounters; an Alpha is crafted by combining a high-QL ordinary Spirit of the matching type with the matching Beta. A QL250 Alpha is 'bumped' toward QL300 by injecting 3-4 more of the same Beta; starting from a QL300 ordinary Spirit often reaches QL300 immediately. Two different Alphas for the same slot can then be combined into a superior Combined Alpha, which takes the QL of the TARGET item - so always make the higher-QL spirit the target. Feet has no combined upgrade.
farmingMethods.noOverequip: Unlike implants, Spirits cannot be over-equipped: ao-universe says the prefix names "indicate a specific level requirement to use. For this reason you cannot over equip these as you could with implants", and the client description on Whispering Spirit (id 218576) says the same. You must genuinely meet the Level and ability requirement of the tier. Two compensating advantages the same guide gives: a Spirit needs NO surgery clinic to install or remove (so you can hot-swap a nano-skill Spirit in to cast something and swap back), and a Spirit buffs more skills than an implant of the same QL. A Spirit also cannot be customised the way an implant can.

steps.mob: unknown

steps.note: Client description says only 'This Spirit is created with synthentic Xan-Tech.' These templates carry the Shadowlands expansion gate (bit 2), NOT the Legacy-of-the-Xan gate (bit 128) that the real Xan spirits carry, and they interpolate QL1-250. No reputable guide covering them was found, so the source is deliberately left unknown rather than guessed. No source states the Shade Spirit version shares that source, so it stays unknown.

steps.mob: Contemplating Spirit / Unrepentant Spirit / Spirit of Disruption (Valley of the Dead), Meditating Spirit / Conflicted Spirit / Spirit of Coercion (Burning Marshes), Relentless Spirit
steps.where: Inferno - Yuttos marshes and the Spirit Dungeons in the Redeemed/Unredeemed temples (camp level 195-205). Named spirit mobs: Contemplating/Unrepentant Spirits and Spirit of Disruption in the ruins north of the Yuttos in the Valley of the Dead; Meditating/Conflicted Spirits and Spirit of Coercion around Burning Marshes (~2035x1185); Relentless Spirits at Burning Marshes 1430x375 (QL200) and Inferno 2230x2170 (QL220).
steps.note: QL200 tier. The named Inferno spirit mobs and their coordinates come from the AO-Universe Inferno 'Spirits Quests' guide, which uses them for a different quest line - they are cited here because they are the documented Spirit-type mobs of that level band, which the Shade guide says drop Spirits.

steps.note: Client description says only 'This Spirit is created with synthentic Xan-Tech.' These templates carry the Shadowlands expansion gate (bit 2), NOT the Legacy-of-the-Xan gate (bit 128) that the real Xan spirits carry, and they interpolate QL1-250. No reputable guide covering them was found, so the source is deliberately left unknown rather than guessed. Second web pass: the allowed sources document only the SYMBIANT counterpart ('Fabricated Symbiants come from cash shop Explorers' Packs'). No source states the Shade Spirit version shares that source, so it stays unknown.
